beats.note: JPL says it stopped sending readable science and engineering data on 14 November 2023.
JPL says a single chip storing part of the flight data subsystem memory was not working. Universe Today puts that at about 3 percent of the memory.

beats.text: The chip could not be repaired.
beats.note: JPL says no single location was large enough to hold the affected code, so the team divided it into sections and stored them in different places.

beats.name: The code move
beats.role: JPL says the new code location was sent on 18 April. On 20 April the team saw that the change had worked.

beats.context: JPL says Voyager 1 is over 15 billion miles from Earth. A radio signal takes about 22.5 hours to reach it.

beats.note: Universe Today gives the launch date as 5 September 1977.

beats.text: A 1977 computer was repaired by changing where its code lives.
